trial_court: 3rd Additional Senior Civil Judge Valsad, Hindu Marriage Petition No. 44 of 2017
case_name: Jolina D/O Anilbhai Patel @ Devanshee vs Pratik Dhiraj Champaneri
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The petitioner filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu marriage Act, 1955 for Restitution of Conjugal rights. The parties got engaged in 2016 and married in 2017. After marriage, the petitioner went to stay with the respondent. The respondent's family adopted an unreasonable approach towards the petitioner, and she was not permitted to fulfill her conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The court shall consider whether it would make it inequitable for it to compel the husband to live with his wife.
legal_principles.held: While deciding a Petition under the said provision, the court shall have to consider whether it would make it inequitable for it to compel the husband to live with his wife.

legal_principles.principle: The court shall consider the conduct of the spouse and the grounds for refusing the restitution of conjugal rights.
legal_principles.held: Moreover, while granting a restitution of conjugal rights the Court will also have to take into consideration the conduct of the spouse and the grounds for refusing the restitution of the conjugal rights

legal_principles.principle: The court shall consider the prejudice likely to be caused to the party suffering the decree.
legal_principles.held: However, it also well settled law that while granting a decree under Section 9 of the HMA, the prejudice likely to be caused to the party suffering the decree must be also considered

legal_principles.principle: The court shall consider the surrounding circumstances depending on each case.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the Court will have to look at the surrounding circumstances depending on each case

outcome.final_order: The judgment and decree dated 09.08.2024 passed in Regular Civil Appeal No. 39 of 2023 has been confirmed, and the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 has been confirmed.
